items.text: Per section 7.2 of the Halverson Logistics master services agreement, penalties for late deliveries are capped at 4% of the monthly invoice and do not apply to delays caused by force majeure. Any dispute must be raised within ten business days of the invoice date.

The library’s new automated returns sorter has been in service for three months, and staff report that mis-sorted items dropped from 2.1% to 0.4%. The sorter uses a barcode scanner and a small robotic arm, and it does not handle oversized art books, which still go through the manual bin. During the pilot, a chatbot on the library website answered basic renewal questions, but it was retired after users found it confusing. The board asked for a full report before any further automation is considered.

During the 2025 performance review cycle, managers should note that ratings of “exceeds expectations” require at least two documented examples of impact beyond the employee’s job description. HR reminds everyone that feedback must be specific and behavior-based, and that any urgent concerns about conduct should be escalated to Employee Relations immediately rather than saved for the review meeting. The calibration sessions are scheduled for the week of March 10.

Under the library’s loan policy, items returned more than 14 days late incur a $2.50 fee, and borrowers with unpaid fees over $10 cannot check out new materials until the balance is cleared. Staff may waive fees for documented medical emergencies at their discretion.

Minutes of the Vendor Review Committee — Q1 2026

Present: R. Okafor (chair), L. Chen, M. Patel, S. Ibrahim. The committee reviewed the renewal terms for the Brightline Analytics contract. Legal noted that the data-processing addendum still lacks a clause on subprocessors, and Brightline has agreed to supply a revised draft by February 28. Finance flagged that the annual increase of 6.5% exceeds the 4% cap negotiated last year, and the chair will raise this with Brightline’s account director.

The committee also discussed the pilot of an AI assistant for contract summarization. Members agreed the tool produced useful first drafts but sometimes missed cross-references, so all summaries will continue to be checked by a lawyer. No decision was made on expanding the pilot.

Action items: L. Chen to circulate the revised addendum; M. Patel to prepare a cost comparison with two alternative vendors; S. Ibrahim to draft a short user guide for the summarization tool. Next meeting: March 14, 10:00, Room 4B.
Please disregard the earlier draft of the performance review template; the final version is now posted on the HR portal under “2025 Review Cycle.”

Library Automation Steering Group — Meeting Notes, 12 November 2025

The group reviewed progress on the RFID self-checkout rollout. All five branches now have at least two self-check machines, and average checkout time has fallen from 3.4 to 1.9 minutes. The chair noted that the vendor’s support response time has been slower than the 24-hour target, and a formal complaint will be sent if the next two tickets are also late.

A proposal to add an AI chatbot to the library catalogue was discussed. The chatbot would answer questions like “is this book available?” and “how do I renew?” using the catalogue API. Several members raised concerns about accessibility and about the chatbot giving wrong answers on fines. It was agreed that a small pilot would run for eight weeks, with a clear disclaimer and a link to a human librarian. No budget was approved yet.

On loans, the group approved extending the standard loan period from 21 to 28 days for print books, effective January. The change will be announced in the newsletter and on the website.

The vendor contract includes a service-level agreement with a 99.9% uptime target and credits of 5% of monthly fees for each hour of downtime beyond that. The customer must notify the vendor of any claim within 30 days of the incident, and the vendor’s liability is limited to fees paid in the preceding 12 months.

For the performance review, employees should submit their self-assessment by January 31. The form asks for three achievements, two areas for development, and one goal for the coming year. Managers will then hold a 45-minute review meeting and enter final ratings in the HR system by February 14. Any requests for a review extension must be sent to HR before January 24.
The library’s automated reminder system sends a text message three days before an item is due and again on the due date. Borrowers can opt out by replying STOP, but standard loan rules still apply.
